chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the ewe, is it more beloved to you or the goat? He (peace be upon him) said: If the goat is male, then it is more beloved to me; and if the goat is female, then the ewe is more beloved to me. He (the narrator) said, I said, So can the castrated one be sacrificed with? He (peace be upon him) said: No, unless there is no other.

And he (peace be upon him) said: The young sheep (jadh') is suitable, but as for the goat, it is not suitable. I said, Is the castrated one more beloved to you or the ewe? He (peace be upon him) said: The suckling is more beloved to me than the ewe, and if it is castrated, then the ewe (is more beloved).

key_terms.الْجَذَعُ: The young sheep (specifically one year old or similar age class)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred order of sacrificial animals in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential hierarchy of sacrificial animals, prioritizing male goats over ewes and young suckling sheep (jadha') over mature females, reflecting the Shia emphasis on selecting the best quality (khayr) for worship. It further clarifies that while castrated animals are generally less preferred, they remain valid if no other option is available, demonstrating the balance between ideal preference and practical necessity in fiqh. These distinctions underscore the scholarly tradition of evaluating animals based on age, gender, and physical condition to ensure the sacrifice is both ritually pure and spiritually significant.
